summary: Three pins surface two problem families: a concrete operational gap (installed Rust binary drifting from source after cli.rs edits) and a strategic failure (V2 widget shipped a plugin contribution-point framework when three concrete tools were requested, compounding across multiple 'not useful' signals instead of pivoting on the first). The cargo/cli.rs issue is a concrete Rust instance of the named binary-rebuild mistake pattern. The V2 story is the highest-signal pin: it names a moment where an 'architecturally professional' choice diverged from the user's grounded need, and the agent repeatedly added surface rather than questioning the premise.

insights.instruction: Watch for this in future events: after any Edit targeting src/cli.rs, flag that the installed binary is now stale and cargo install must run before claiming the CLI change is live.

When a user says 'not useful' after a feature ship, do not add more surface. Stop and audit whether the architectural premise matches the user's actual grounded need. Concrete user requests are not prompts to generalize into a framework.

summary: Three pins from 2026-05-29 split across two problem surfaces: a catastrophic compound failure in the Versable frontend agent session exposing a performative-self-criticism anti-pattern and a hinter pipeline gap, and two structural bugs in i-dream itself where both the daily digest and the interactive audit generate fresh data instead of reading authoritative persisted state. The Versable pin is the most complex — it names five known live slugs that still failed to correct in-session behavior, suggesting enforcement surface (UserPromptSubmit) is insufficient. The i-dream pins share a root cause worth associating: consumers that silently discard persisted state in favor of re-generation.

A single high-signal pin describes a cross-cutting false-positive class in raw-command-string-scanning hooks: guards that match dangerous tokens anywhere in a shell invocation string will trip on documentation prose, RCA content, and here-doc bodies that discuss the very commands being blocked. The cli-gating subsystem already solved this (quoted-string awareness + 150 tests), but safe-delete and guard-system-dir-writes have not adopted the fix. The actionable dream output is a refactoring proposal and a shared helper extraction to unify all five scanning hooks under the same command-position-aware parser.

insights.instruction: Extract a shared `is_token_in_command_position(token, argv)` helper — reusing cli-gating's existing quoted-string and heredoc-body parsing logic — and thread it through safe-delete.sh, guard-system-dir-writes.sh, comment-hygiene, and env-access hooks. ci-gating's 150-test suite becomes the regression harness for all five.
When reviewing any new guard/hook proposal, apply the same context-awareness bar as for ADR exceptions: ask 'does this matcher understand the grammatical position of the token, or only its presence?'

Add a hook-authoring checklist item to PLACEMENT.md or scripts/hooks/README.md: 'Does this hook scan raw command strings? If yes, does it use the shared command-position parser? If no shared parser exists yet, implement one in lib/ and adopt it here.'

summary: Two pins from 2026-06-19 capture the graduation arc of the ai-smell-prose-against-stored-voice S3 atone event (mist-20260619-194539-c9) into rules/audience-aware-writing.md, which is now live in CLAUDE.md Tier-0. The graduation rule side is complete; the mechanical enforcement side — Stop-stage prose hook prop-20260619-194931-ba — remains status:open. Historical precedent from source-comment-hygiene (same class of advisory rule, same account) and the Versable hinter-failure session (pin-20260529152121-e6) both point toward the same conclusion: the advisory rule alone will not correct the pattern under pressure.

A single pin from 2026-06-21 grounds itself in a concrete ARG_MAX bug caught by immediately exercising a new vision command against real data the instant the model finished downloading. The latent theme is not the bug itself but its cause: the user's 'reliability over performance' evaluation axis drove the immediate exercise and surfaced what static inspection would have missed. This preference refines and unifies three existing patterns — exercise-based-verification, structure-over-one-shotting, efficacy-over-speed — into an explicit trust hierarchy that should graduate into global memory.

insights.instruction: When any local-models bin/ tool processes image files or large text blobs, test it with a real-sized input before declaring done. Shell arg limits are silent — no warning, just truncation or ENOMEM. Pattern to watch: jq --arg combined with binary-to-base64 output or large model responses.
Audit bin/probe and any new bin/ commands added to local-models for the large-buffer-through-shell-args pattern. If found, apply the Python-inline or stdin-pipe pattern used in bin/see:82-103.

summary: The two new pins form a paired case study in the same failure class. The first (pin-20260624080929-6d) documents a 3rd S3 recurrence of speculative-abstractions despite a live rule, atone hints, and previous corrections, plus a double-recording slip from misreading background CLI silence as process death. The second (pin-20260624205747-54) shows the structural inverse: a design → adversarial-skeptic → cheap empirical test loop killing the same class of over-build before any code was written, with the three relevant atone slugs used as a predictive checklist rather than an after-the-fact guardrail. Together they reveal that slugs are diagnostic at design time but not corrective mid-session, and that an empirical test is what converts skeptic opinion into falsifiable fact.

The pinned insight captures a multi-rung integration ladder for using local-models as a decoupled Claude worker fleet. Cross-referencing docs/03 and docs/07 reveals the architectural decision is already resolved: deterministic pipeline (Claude conducts, q workers execute scoped single calls, Judge gate verifies) is canonical — model-driven loops are unanimously rejected by MAGI. The pin's open question about direct-calls vs Claude-called vs mix is a false dichotomy; the real invariant is whether the local model self-directs (rejected) vs executes a predetermined scope (approved).

insights.instruction: Before implementing any rung of the integration ladder, verify each q worker call has a PREDETERMINED SCOPE defined by the orchestrator (Claude), not by the local model. If the local model decides what file to read next or what tool to call next, it is the rejected MODEL-DRIVEN LOOP pattern.

When implementing docs/07 Phase-1, ensure the weekly self-audit emits events compatible with the atone JSONL schema (id, slug, severity, issue, fix fields) so i-dream can ingest fleet quality signals alongside session-level corrections without a schema adapter.

When routing a task, apply the split explicitly: HIGH-VOLUME + LOW-STAKES-PER-CALL + VERIFIABLE (review, recon, mechanical transforms) goes to local worker fleet; hard reasoning, design, synthesis stays with cloud sub-agents where peak intelligence justifies cost and throttle risk.

summary: The new pin describes a deferred architectural decision: generalize the claude-instances dashboard from a hard-coded Claude provider to an agentic-runner × model session dashboard. The pin already completed the options assessment (cheapest = separate lm/q calls panel; cleanest = provider interface abstraction) and explicitly defers the build choice to the weekly audit. This is a rare 'the thinking is done, the gate is a calendar event' shape — the useful dream work is surfacing the cross-association with pin-20260702191100-51 (worker-fleet integration) and flagging the concrete design invariant the cleanest option must not violate.

insights.instruction: The worker-fleet pin resolved orchestration architecture (Claude conducts, q workers execute predetermined scope). The dashboard pin is the observability layer for the same ecosystem. When building option (2)'s provider interface, the 'enumerate procs by pattern; parse tail → {model,state,activity}' contract maps directly to the fleet's worker-call JSONL schema — both surfaces read the same signal (model id, state, activity). Design them to share a parser rather than duplicating the transcript-tail logic. Cross-reference docs/07-implementation.md for the JSONL field names before authoring the provider interface.

insights.name: provider-coupling-in-observability-tooling
insights.instruction: scan.sh:492-521 hard-codes three provider assumptions: (1) binary name is exactly 'claude', (2) transcript dir is ~/.claude/projects, (3) a session == one transcript file. Before adding local-models or codex support, extract these three assumptions into a ProviderDef struct {proc_pattern, transcript_dir, session_glob, tail_parser} with the Claude implementation as the reference. Any new runner is then a new ProviderDef entry, not a new code path. If a runner's transcript format is incompatible with the tail_parser contract, implement a thin adapter — never branch on provider name inside the core scan loop.

insights.rationale: This pin is the second instance of a pin that says 'options assessed, decision deferred to weekly audit.' The pattern suggests the weekly audit needs an explicit agenda item: 'pins with deferred build decisions.' Without a calendar-backed queue, deferred decisions decay without resolution. Consider adding a recurring 'resolve deferred pins' step to the weekly audit ritual.

insights.name: option-1-cheapest-path-viable-now
insights.instruction: Option (1) — an lm/q calls panel reading ~/Code/local-models JSONL histories — is buildable today without any provider interface refactor because one-shot calls are not live sessions (separate panel, no proc enumeration needed). If the weekly audit decision leans toward proving value before committing to the cleanest option, implement option (1) as a standalone panel first. Verify ~/Code/local-models JSONL history path and field names before authoring the panel (cross-reference docs/07-implementation.md:1-50 per pin-20260702191100-51).

summary: Three pins from 2026-07-10/11 surface a shared epistemological pattern: in each session, a proposed build turned out to be unnecessary or wrong once the underlying platform/data was actually measured or audited. The IPC investigation killed an elegant architecture pre-build by measuring its key premise against a real corpus; the imagine CLI session found 28 existing backend tools rendering the gap purely a wiring problem; the ghostty V3 fork was retired the same day because the compositor already covered it. Two graduation candidates emerge: a standing extension-points-over-forks preference and a concrete imagine subcommand wiring proposal.

insights.instruction: When a proposed design depends on a behavioral ratio (fraction of X that are Y, hit rate, fraction answerable), collect a real sample from the relevant corpus and measure BEFORE committing to a build plan. A positive feasibility verdict under an unmeasured premise is not a build authorization.

Before scoping a net-new capability: audit the existing toolchain at depth. For local model tools, check the underlying venv/lib. For terminal extensions, check the compositor/plugin layer. Lead with the inventory; only scope new build after confirming the gap is real at the platform level, not just the CLI surface.

For any future IPC design iteration: (1) delivery guarantee is the primary lever — the Monitor-wakes-idle spike is the next unproven step; (2) do not optimize query-API shape until delivery works; (3) re-measure traffic composition if the corpus grows past ~30 samples, as 9% state-answerable on 11 samples is a small-n finding. Buildable now: durable parking + desk-name discovery (data-independent wins from the retired Desk design).

summary: Two pins from 2026-07-14 surface paired failure modes in mutation-testing workflow and the skeptical-reviewer sub-agent persona. The mutation pin reveals that git checkout during a live mutation loop silently destroys uncommitted work, and output filtering below the pass/fail line makes the mutation proof unreadable — both errors combined to render the A1 mutation round meaningless without detection. The skeptical-reviewer pin exposes a gap between the sub-agent-outputs rule (which governs persistence) and audience-aware-writing (which governs prose voice): neither currently binds the persona output contract to produce findings a human can parse without the code open.

insights.instruction: Before any mutation loop: snapshot the target file with cp to /tmp or a named scratchpad. After each run, restore with cp -f and verify with diff -q. Never use git checkout/restore on a file with uncommitted changes. Never pipe test output through a filter that drops the pass/fail summary line — the raw suite output is the proof.

Add a self-contained-finding output contract to skeptical-reviewer.md. Gate: before dispatching any auditor persona sub-agent, verify its persona file has an output-contract section requiring jargon-free self-contained findings for a human reader.

summary: Three new pins cluster around two related failure modes: agents trusting cheap proxies (stale derived artifacts, heuristic-only hooks) instead of running the actual discriminating check, and multi-agent scoped-directive divergence where no reconciliation channel exists except the human. The evidence-hierarchy finding (pin-96) is the sharpest: a review report is an index, never a source of facts, yet agents habitually treat the cheapest evidence as ground truth. The hook-calibration finding (pin-b8) and the directive-divergence finding (pin-bb) each demand a new rule or structural change rather than a nudge.

insights.instruction: Watch for: two-agent sessions on shared artifacts, scoped labeling or naming directives, one agent relaying a correction it received from another. Before acting on a peer-relayed constraint, verify it independently against the owner's original directive rather than trusting the relay. This is a new failure mode not covered by existing multi-agent coordination rules — the human's intent was coherent; the agents' extrapolations were not.

When adding a new rule to this family, frame it around the availability of a cheap discriminating check: name what the check IS and why it is being skipped. Rules that only describe the failure mode without naming the cheap check that prevents it are underspecified — the agent has no action to take at the moment the slip would occur.

Before the IPC spike (Monitor wake test), add one design question to the scope: can the parking/desk state store include a 'last-directive-hash' per project that both agents can read before extrapolating from a scoped directive? If the hash diverges from what either agent expects, that is the detector. This is a one-field addition to the durable parking design and costs nothing to name now.
